hero.title: Panackal Bhadrakali Devi Temple
hero.desc: A sacred abode of Maa Bhadrakali, the supreme form of Shakti — fierce yet compassionate, destroyer of evil, protector of the devoted. Nestled in Kerala's sacred landscape, this temple has blessed generations of devotees with grace and divine protection.
hero.timing: Morning: 5:00 AM – 1:00 PM  |  Evening: 5:30 PM – 9:00 PM
hero.timingNote: Special poojas may alter timings on festival days.

deity.p: Bhadrakali — the benevolent aspect of Kali — is worshipped here in the traditional Kerala Tantric tradition. She is depicted with eight arms, each holding a sacred weapon, standing upon the asura Darika.

history.p: The temple traces its origins over five centuries ago, consecrated by the Panackal family in accordance with Tantric rites of the Kalari tradition. The main idol is swayambhu — self-manifested.

reach.p: Located in Kerala. Nearest bus stop: Panackal Junction (0.3 km). Nearest railway: Ernakulam (42 km). Parking available on the eastern side of the temple complex.

items: Women: Saree or churidar with dupatta
No shorts or sleeveless attire inside the sanctum

n1.title: Sivarathri Special Pooja – Feb 26
n1.body: Special Mahashivarathri celebrations will be held on Feb 26. Ashtayamam from 6 AM through midnight. Devotees are welcome to participate in all eight sessions.

n2.title: Temple Renovation – North Entrance Closed
n2.body: The north entrance of the temple will be closed from Feb 22 to March 10 due to ongoing renovation work. Kindly use the east entrance during this period.

n3.title: Online Offerings Now Available
n3.body: Devotees can now book and pay for Vazhipadu (offerings) online. Your name and birth star will be announced during the pooja.

n4.title: Meena Bharani Festival – March 14
n4.body: The annual Meena Bharani festival — the grandest celebration — will be held on March 14. Special poojas from 4 AM. Prasadam distribution at noon.

o1.name: Pushpanjali
o1.desc: Flower offering with chanting of sacred mantras.

o2.name: Nilavilakku Pooja
o2.desc: Brass lamp offering symbolising Bhadrakali's divine light.

o3.name: Nivedyam (Aval & Sharkkara)
o3.desc: Traditional offering of flattened rice with jaggery.

o4.name: Manjal Thettiyathu
o4.desc: Turmeric-soaked threads for protection and prosperity.

o5.name: Deepa Pooja (101 Diyas)
o5.desc: Lighting of 101 earthen lamps encircling the sanctum.

o6.name: Kuruthikala (Symbolic)
o6.desc: Symbolic traditional blood offering; fully sanctioned.

o7.name: Thalamudiyatu (Chendamelam)
o7.desc: Percussion ensemble dedicated to the Goddess — classical Kerala drum.

o8.name: Poomudu & Vastra Samarpanam
o8.desc: Fresh flower garlands and sacred cloth offered to the Goddess.

o9.name: Ashtabhuja Archana
o9.desc: Archana to all eight arms of Bhadrakali with 108 names.
